figure.purpose: The credit total on the Overview. One per screen.

display.purpose: The one prompt or title per screen.

title.purpose: Choice row names and the transcript panel title.

title-row.purpose: Ranked picks and collapsible requirement sections.

lede.purpose: One or two soft sentences under the display line, max 44ch.

label.purpose: Tabs, header name, legends, requirement group names.

control.purpose: Chips, toggles, grade bands, status words.

meta.purpose: The soft second line of any row.

fine.purpose: The privacy line and table column heads.

shadows.name: open-ring
shadows.purpose: Draws the amber outline of an open meter segment. Not a shadow. The system has no drop shadows.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for arrival and control state changes.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: Runs once when a setup screen or portal section arrives.

motion.name: control

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active state of primary and secondary buttons.

components.css: .ds-side ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 0.25rem; } .ds-tab { font-family: var(--font); width: 100%; min-height: 44px; padding: 0.15rem 0.5rem 0; border: 0; border-radius: 12px; background: none; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.95rem; color: var(--soft); white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s var(--ease), color 0.15s var(--ease); } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--ink); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--blue); outline-offset: -3px; } .ds-tab[aria-current="page"] { background: var(--green-tint); color: var(--green); }

narrative.overview:
Dragon Credit Map looks like a clean ruled ledger a student keeps for themselves: white ground, one warm paper tone for the places where something is handed over or stated, warm near-black ink, and a single green that says "this is the tool, and this is the next step". Results are not boxed. They sit in ruled lists that open under a 2px ink rule and separate with 1px hairlines, so a long checklist reads as one page of a ledger, not a wall of tiles.

The voice is large, plain, and short. Each setup screen opens with one very heavy full-sentence prompt, and the portal Overview opens with one very large number. Everything below those is quiet: soft grey supporting text, small bold labels, tabular figures wherever hours or counts appear. Meaning that matters (earned, planned, open, take at college) is carried three ways at once: a text label, a shape, and a blue or amber color.

Both themes are designed. The light theme is white and paper; the dark theme is a warm near-black with the same roles, re-tuned so every text pair keeps its contrast. The line map direction that was built first and replaced is the confirmed anti-reference: no route rails, no interchange capsules.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, warm paper second surface, warm ink. No cool greys.
One green for theme and action. Blue and amber for status. Red only on the dragon mark.
Ruled lists under a 2px ink rule in place of result cards.
One heavy sans family, Overpass, from weight 400 to 900, self-hosted.
Status is a label plus a shape plus a color, never a color alone.
Phone first. Every control is at least 44px tall.

rules.name: The Blue And Amber Rule
rules.body: Status never relies on red against green. Good or counted is blue, needs attention is amber, and every status also carries a text label and a shape.

rules.name: The Green Is Not A Verdict Rule
rules.body: Green is the theme and the action color. It never means passed, earned, covered, or correct. If a state needs a verdict, it gets blue or amber.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red appears on the dragon mark only. It is never an error color; errors and warnings are amber.

rules.name: The Counting Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number a student might compare (hours, counts, course codes, scores, ranks) is set in tabular figures.

rules.name: The Sentence Rule
rules.body: Every heading and label is sentence case. There are no uppercase labels and no letter-spaced small caps anywhere in the build.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: Copy is plain and short, and interface text contains no em dashes. Use a period, a comma, or a colon.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts off the page. If something needs separating, rule it or put it on paper.

rules.name: The Shape Carries It Rule
rules.body: A status mark must be readable in one color. Circle, half circle, ring, and square are never swapped or reused for anything else.

dos: Do give every status a text label, a shape, and blue or amber. Check each new status in greyscale.
Do use the ink fill as the single selected treatment for toggles, grade bands, score buttons, and filter chips.
Do open result lists with a 2px ink rule and divide rows with 1px lines.
Do keep one display line or one figure per screen, at weight 900, with a soft lede under it.
Do set hours, counts, codes, scores, and ranks in tabular figures.
Do design every new surface in both themes, using the token pairs; never a raw hex in a component.
Do keep every tap target at least 44px tall and keep the visible 3px focus outline.
Do self-host every asset. The page loads nothing from another origin.
Do write copy as short plain sentences in sentence case.
donts: Don't let red against green carry meaning anywhere.
Don't use green for a verdict (earned, covered, passed). Green is theme and action only.
Don't use red outside the dragon mark, including for errors.
Don't add a second selected style for a pressed control.
Don't put results in a grid of identical stat cards, and don't box ledger rows.
Don't bring back the line map: no route rails, no interchange capsules.
Don't use an em dash in interface text.
Don't add comments to any code file. Explain design decisions here, not in the source.
Don't use NCSSM, UNC, or NC State logos, colors, wordmarks, or mascots. Name them in plain text.
Don't store anything or call another origin to achieve a visual effect.
